key_insight: Scaling test-time compute in embodied planners is not automatically better: it raises latency, token usage, and FLOPs, but the gains in downstream success can be uneven and quickly diminish. The paper’s core message is that embodied agents need to spend compute more selectively—on the right decisions, at the right time.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge of how to allocate limited test-time compute in Vision-Language-Model-based embodied planning so that performance improves without making systems too slow, expensive, or impractical for real-world deployment.
method: Analyzes when increasing test-time compute helps versus when it produces diminishing returns in embodied planning.
Focuses on deciding where compute should be spent across planning steps or decision points rather than uniformly scaling all reasoning.
Frames compute allocation as a deployment constraint tradeoff among success rate, latency, token usage, and FLOPs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights that better embodied performance is not just about larger models or more inference-time reasoning. It provides a practical lens for building faster, more efficient agents that can still achieve frontier-level behavior in real environments.
visual_elements: A tradeoff chart showing success rate vs. latency/token/FLOP cost as test-time compute increases.
A pipeline diagram of an embodied planner with highlighted decision points where compute can be allocated.
An icon-based comparison of 'more compute everywhere' vs. 'targeted compute where needed'.
A diminishing-returns curve illustrating how gains flatten as compute scales up.
paper_title: DIRECT: When and Where Should You Allocate Test-Time Compute in Embodied Planners?
paper_authors: Jadelynn Dao, Milan Ganai, Yasmina Abukhadra, Ajay Sridhar, Mozhgan Nasr Azadani
